comparison: Both evaluate TMD measurements (C7, C10-C24) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes quantitative rigor and statistical testing, while peer reviewers praise the 'excellent combination of scanning and histological data.' Peer result also includes C123 (convergent evidence claim), showing broader grouping.

Perfect agreement on claims C31-C40 regarding ratfish neural arches. Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval highlights the convergence of multiple complementary techniques, while peer reviewers characterize this as part of 'compelling' new data with 'excellent combination' of methods.

Perfect agreement on claims C41-C49 regarding trabecular mineralization patterns. Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes the comparative analysis across three species, while peer reviewers describe this as 'very valuable and unique comparative study' with no specific critiques.

Strong agreement on claims C50-C61 regarding cap zones and spokes. Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval highlights the novel 3D segmentation achievement, while peer reviewers praise 'state of the art and complementary approaches.' Peer result also includes C118-C120 (spatial correlations), showing overlap with OpenEval R10.

Perfect agreement on claims C62-C73 regarding centra characterization. Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes convergent evidence from multiple techniques, while peer reviewers note 'excellent combination of scanning and histological data' as part of compelling new findings.

Both address developmental comparisons (C75-C85) and evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval focuses on the developmental series data, while peer reviewers accept the underlying observations but raise conceptual concerns about paedomorphism interpretation (addressed in R7). Peer result includes convergent evidence claims (C122, C124-C125, C127-C128) that OpenEval addresses separately in R8.

Both evaluate paedomorphism claims (C129, C131) as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes the inference requires additional evidence beyond current data and is appropriately qualified. Peer reviewer explicitly questions whether development in extant holocephalans can be established as derived, emphasizing uncertainty about relationships, though notes this is 'a point of discussion, not a requirement.'

Both address major evolutionary conclusions (C8, C98-C102) and evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes synthesis of multiple lines of evidence, while peer reviewers state the study 'provides the basis for an in-depth discussion' and will 'likely impact several fields.' Peer result includes additional evolutionary claims (C103, C105-C113, C139-C140) that OpenEval addresses separately in R9 and R13.
